chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:

Concerning a man who accuses another man of zinā, he said: “He is to be flogged according to the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله.”
He said: And I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who accuses a young slave-girl, so he said: “He is not flogged unless she has reached maturity or has nearly reached it.”

key_terms.الزِّنَى: illicit sexual intercourse; the charge being alleged
key_terms.سُنَّةِ نَبِيِّهِ: the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of His Prophet as legal authority
key_terms.قَارَبَتْ: she has come near to maturity
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: the Book of Allah, meaning the Qur'an as legal authority
key_terms.يَقْذِفُ: to accuse falsely, specifically with an allegation of zinā
key_terms.يُجْلَدُ: he is to be flogged as the prescribed punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on falsely accusing someone of zinā, and does it apply when the accused is a young girl?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on false accusation of zinā, stating that the accuser is subject to flogging in accordance with the Book of Allah and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. It also clarifies that in the case of accusing a young girl, the prescribed punishment applies only if she has reached, or nearly reached, maturity.
